correctness.rationale: The conditional permutation and directed rooted-forest decomposition is standard. Matrix-tree gives k n^(n-k-1) forests with k fixed cyclic roots; deleting r specified terminal nonroots and reattaching them gives k(n-r)^(n-k-1), hence every factorial moment. Strictly decreasing conditional mean proves finite anticovariance, and an independent one-terminal deletion computes exact covariance. Uniform Rayleigh/Gaussian bounds justify taking the second-order expansion through mixed moments; the occupancy variance establishes the correlation constant. The packaged Python verifier exhaustively counts all n^n functions at n=2,...,7 in exact rational arithmetic and checks every conditional stratum, with numerical larger-n diagnostics; no infinite proof is inferred from finite tests.

Hansen–Jaworski 2010 theorems displayed in the accessible primary pages condition component size on cyclic vertex counts; no displayed result determines indegree-zero count dependence.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The forest-volume formula has broader combinatorial coverage and yields the elementary conditional-event counting after a specialization; this ingredient is explicitly prior. The assessed mixed covariance asymptotic additionally needs distributional weighting across random cyclic root counts and a second-order cancellation argument. No inspected broader result was shown to imply those sharp mixed conclusions; full priority checking remains limited by one inaccessible plausible source.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Separate literature implications from titles: fixed-root decomposition does imply the initial counting step and is not new; conditioned component-size and cyclic-depth theorems do not identify the indegree-zero statistic; stratum and closer equivalences fail by definition. An older unstated specialization or stronger general result is a residual historical-priority risk.

originality.rationale: Accessible primary literature supplies standard uniform rooted-forest conditioning and individual marginal statistics, but no inspected claim covers the complete conditional indegree-zero factorial-moment family together with finite strict sign and its nonzero square-root covariance constant. The accessible close papers address cyclic depths, component sizes, cyclic strata or another terminal-closer statistic; their stated theorems do not entail the mixed terminal-count result as stated. Potential specialization of a general forest enumerator and a nonaccessible forest-leaf paper remain genuine historical priority uncertainties.
residual_risks: The full primary text of Mylläri (2002) was not available; it may contain a related conditional forest-leaf distribution or stronger general theorem.

Pitman (2001) and older general forest generating-function results imply the counting ingredient and may allow a routine derivation of parts of the conditional law; an equivalent combined asymptotic result might be implicit in older specialization.
A negative search result and independent finite enumeration do not certify mathematical priority. No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Cyclic vertices and terminal vertices are natural complementary functional-graph observables with distinct scaling. Their conditional relationship displays cancellation of the potentially order-sqrt(n) mean displacement, yielding an exact monotone law and a nonzero square-root covariance constant despite asymptotically vanishing correlation. The sharp mixed result supplies a motivated dependence benchmark not fixed by separate marginal laws; it is not presented as a reproof of the general forest enumerator.
